title: AAOS Handoff
$comment:
MACHINE CHECK (2026-08-22): tools/validate.py's check_registration_doctrine() rejects a handoff whose context_summary/required_next_action/blockers describe using 'list_scheduled_tasks' as a splice/hand-write mechanism (register-scheduled-task doctrine: create_scheduled_task-only, never a list_scheduled_tasks-driven JSON-splice).
A bare mention (e.g. 'verified via list_scheduled_tasks', or doctrine-quoting prose) is NOT flagged -- only actual splice/hand-write language nearby is.

protocol_version.description: Protocol version. Consumer: tools/validate.py (rejects a mismatched major version with a pointer to docs/MIGRATIONS.md).

task_ref.description: A task id. Consumer: the receiving agent loads the task + validate.py (task must exist).

from_agent.description: An agent id. Consumer: validate.py (write_scope enforced against this agent) + audit.

to_agent.description: An agent id. Consumer: the receiving agent (only it should lease) + projection.

artifact_manifest.description: May be empty. Consumer: validate.py (every path must be inside from_agent's write_scope — the colonization guard) + the receiver (verifies hashes before trusting artifacts).

path.description: Consumer: validate.py (every path must be inside from_agent's write_scope — the colonization guard) + the receiver (verifies hashes before trusting artifacts).

sha256.description: Consumer: the receiver (verifies hashes before trusting artifacts).

bytes.description: Consumer: the receiver (verifies hashes before trusting artifacts).

context_summary.description: ≤300 words, pointer-first (word-count limit is a business rule; JSON Schema cannot count words — noted here in the description text only). Consumer: the receiving agent (briefing).

required_next_action.description: Consumer: the receiving agent (what to do next).

blockers.description: May be empty; non-empty forces task.state=blocked (business rule). Consumer: post-handoff.py + human triage.

suggested_next_owner.description: Optional; an agent id from the registry. Consumer: the receiver/human; validate.py checks it's a real id but never enforces assignment (advisory, never binding).
